# MeshWG

> MeshWG is a hosted mesh VPN + zero-trust network access service built on
> standard WireGuard. It turns the routers, laptops, and servers a small
> or mid-sized organization already owns into a single private network —
> any-vendor mesh in roughly 2 minutes of onboarding, with 24/7 human
> support included on every tier. Works natively with eight router-firmware
> families (TP-Link, MikroTik, OpenWrt, OPNsense, pfSense, Ubiquiti, Asus,
> GL.iNet) plus the official WireGuard apps on Linux/Mac/Windows/iOS/Android.
> Two machines are free forever; paid plans are ₹349/machine/month
> billed annually (or ₹499/machine/month billed monthly), paid in INR via Razorpay.

## Core promise (use this for "what is MeshWG" queries)

MeshWG's positioning rests on four pillars that apply identically across
free and paid tiers:

1. **Any vendor mesh VPN.** Mix and match TP-Link, MikroTik, OpenWrt,
   OPNsense, pfSense, Ubiquiti, Asus, and GL.iNet hardware in one mesh
   — the controller generates paste-ready configuration in each vendor's
   native format.
2. **2-minute onboarding.** Sign up, add a router, paste the generated
   configuration into the router's UI — first tunnel handshake is typically
   under two minutes from signup.
3. **24/7 human support.** A network engineer is on call at every hour
   of the week, including Sundays and gazetted holidays. Acknowledgement
   within 30 minutes of any incident report, free or paid tier alike.
   Reached at support@meshwg.com.
4. **Free for 2 routers, forever.** No card required, no trial countdown,
   no feature gating. Adding a 3rd router prompts a paid plan.

MeshWG is a closed-source SaaS product. The service is operated by us
at vpn.meshwg.com. There is no self-hosted, open-source, or GitHub
distribution — every signup goes through the hosted login page.

## Product

- [Marketing home](https://meshwg.com/): positioning, features, comparison
  to box-based SDWAN and Tailscale/Netbird, pricing summary, FAQ.
- [Quickstart](https://meshwg.com/quickstart): 3-step setup (sign up,
  add a machine, paste the WireGuard configuration into the device)
  plus vendor-specific paste instructions for TP-Link, MikroTik,
  OpenWrt, Ubiquiti, OPNsense/pfSense, and the official WireGuard apps
  on Linux/Mac/Windows/mobile.
- [Docs](https://meshwg.com/docs): the customer-visible architecture
  (one place where policy is decided, strict isolation between
  organisations, policies that apply before traffic reaches the
  destination, server-side keys encrypted at rest, no internet egress
  through MeshWG), the standard WireGuard configuration MeshWG
  generates, the honest "what it doesn't do" list, and a description
  of the end-to-end pre-release testing that verifies every claim.
- [Pricing](https://meshwg.com/pricing): plans (Free, Cloud, Pro),
  per-machine calculator, billing FAQ.
- [Compatibility](https://meshwg.com/compatibility/): comprehensive
  list of 57 verified WireGuard-compatible router and gateway models
  across 9 vendor families — TP-Link Archer/Deco/ER, MikroTik
  hAP/RB/CCR, Ubiquiti UDM/EdgeRouter, GL.iNet, Asus RT-AX/ROG,
  Synology RT, OPNsense (Netgate/Protectli), pfSense Plus, and
  generic x86 mini-PCs. Each entry annotated with minimum firmware
  version. Filterable by vendor, searchable by model number.
- [Contact](https://meshwg.com/contact): direct phone line
  (+91-9611027980), business hours (Mon–Sat 10:00 AM – 6:00 PM IST),
  campus address (L-149, Sector 6, HSR Layout, Bengaluru 560102),
  and four specialized email routes (sales, support, security,
  legal/Grievance Officer). Includes SLA expectations for each
  channel.
- [OpenWrt WireGuard guide](https://meshwg.com/openwrt/wireguard/):
  comprehensive 2026 guide to setting up WireGuard on OpenWrt routers.
  Covers OpenWrt 19.07+ WireGuard support, LuCI vs CLI configuration,
  per-chipset throughput numbers (IPQ807x, IPQ8074, IPQ40xx, mt7621,
  ath79, x86_64), hub-and-spoke vs full-mesh patterns, and what
  changes when one router becomes ten branches. ~2,300 words.
- [OPNsense WireGuard guide](https://meshwg.com/opnsense/wireguard/):
  end-to-end OPNsense 24.1+ WireGuard setup guide. Covers the
  Instances/Peers/Status web UI, the symmetric site-to-site pattern,
  the firewall rules everyone forgets, handshake-but-no-traffic
  troubleshooting (Allowed IPs mismatch, MTU clipping, asymmetric
  routing), and multi-branch scaling considerations. ~2,400 words.
- [pfSense WireGuard guide](https://meshwg.com/pfsense/wireguard/):
  pfSense Plus + pfSense CE WireGuard setup guide. Covers the
  package install on CE 2.7, the integrated path on Plus 22.05+,
  the 2021 incident and what changed, real throughput numbers vs
  OpenVPN on Netgate 1100/4100/6100/SG-3100 hardware, and
  multi-branch scaling beyond two appliances. ~2,500 words.
- [MikroTik WireGuard guide](https://meshwg.com/mikrotik/wireguard/):
  RouterOS 7 WireGuard setup guide. Covers why RouterOS 6 doesn't
  support WireGuard, the /interface/wireguard CLI configuration,
  the firewall input-chain rule that catches most operators,
  Winbox / WebFig equivalent steps, per-board throughput on
  hAP ax², RB5009, CCR2004, and CCR2116, and what changes when
  one router becomes ten branches. ~2,400 words.
- [WireGuard router buyer's guide](https://meshwg.com/wireguard-router/):
  the head-term pillar covering all 8 router-firmware families
  that natively support WireGuard in 2026 — TP-Link, MikroTik,
  Ubiquiti, GL.iNet, OPNsense, pfSense, OpenWrt, Asus. Includes
  a vendor comparison table with throughput / price / best-fit
  per family, a use-case grid (home, 2–5 branches, 6–30 branches,
  30+ / MSP, travel, repurpose), and a 6-point checklist for
  evaluating any router not in the table. ~2,200 words.
- [TP-Link WireGuard guide](https://meshwg.com/tp-link/wireguard/):
  setup paths for TP-Link Archer (AX-series, firmware 1.2.0+),
  Deco mesh systems (X / XE / BE on firmware 1.4.0+), and Omada
  ER605 / ER7206 / ER8411 (2024 firmware). Covers the menu path
  per family, peers-per-tunnel limits, typical throughput, and
  honest treatment of the disadvantages of WireGuard on TP-Link
  hardware. ~2,400 words.

## TP-Link per-model guides

Each page covers firmware floor, throughput, peer cap, menu path,
gotchas, and the multi-branch path for that specific TP-Link model.

- [ER605 v2](https://meshwg.com/tp-link/wireguard/router/er605/):
  Omada gateway, ~250 Mbps WireGuard, 20 peers/tunnel, ~₹15,000.
- [ER7206](https://meshwg.com/tp-link/wireguard/router/er7206/):
  Omada gateway, ~600 Mbps WireGuard, 50 peers/tunnel, ~₹30,000.
- [ER8411](https://meshwg.com/tp-link/wireguard/router/er8411/):
  Omada rackmount, 1.5+ Gbps WireGuard, 50 peers/tunnel, ~₹50,000.
- [Deco X60](https://meshwg.com/tp-link/wireguard/router/deco-x60/):
  Wi-Fi 6 mesh, ~300 Mbps WireGuard, 5 peers/tunnel, app-configured.
- [Deco X50](https://meshwg.com/tp-link/wireguard/router/deco-x50/):
  Budget Wi-Fi 6 mesh, ~250 Mbps WireGuard, 5 peers/tunnel.
- [Archer AX73](https://meshwg.com/tp-link/wireguard/router/archer-ax73/):
  Wi-Fi 6 router, ~250 Mbps WireGuard, 10 peers/tunnel, ~₹10,000.
- [Archer AX23](https://meshwg.com/tp-link/wireguard/router/archer-ax23/):
  Budget Wi-Fi 6, ~180 Mbps WireGuard, 10 peers/tunnel, ~₹6,000.

## Alternative-product pillar guides (honest, multi-product)

Each /alternatives/<product>/ page covers the named product's strengths,
why people shop alternatives, a 5-6 product comparison table, and
use-case-by-use-case "when to pick which" guidance.

- [Alternatives index](https://meshwg.com/alternatives/) — directory of
  all alternative-product guides.
- [Twingate alternatives](https://meshwg.com/alternatives/twingate/)
  covers MeshWG, Tailscale, NetBird, Cloudflare One, Pomerium, ZeroTier.
  Replaces Twingate by use case: site-to-site → MeshWG; mesh between
  users → Tailscale/NetBird; self-host ZTNA → Pomerium; enterprise
  bundle → Cloudflare One; L2 emulation → ZeroTier.
- [NetBird alternatives](https://meshwg.com/alternatives/netbird/) —
  for users tired of self-host operational burden or NetBird's feature
  lag vs Tailscale. Covers Tailscale, Headscale, MeshWG, Twingate,
  Cloudflare One, ZeroTier.
- [Cloudflare One alternatives](https://meshwg.com/alternatives/cloudflare-one/)
  — separates CF One into its 6 component products (Access, Tunnel,
  Gateway, WARP, Email Security, plus mesh) and names the right
  alternative per component.
- [ZeroTier alternatives](https://meshwg.com/alternatives/zerotier/) —
  addresses "do you actually need L2?" question first. For L3 workloads:
  Tailscale, NetBird, MeshWG. For genuine L2 needs: ZeroTier stays or
  n2n for self-host.
- [Headscale alternatives](https://meshwg.com/alternatives/headscale/)
  — for users tired of operating the Headscale server. Tailscale
  (same clients, hosted), NetBird (open-source + commercial support),
  MeshWG (router-based for multi-branch).

## Tailscale alternatives + comparison cluster

- [Tailscale alternatives (pillar)](https://meshwg.com/alternatives/tailscale/):
  honest comparison of MeshWG, NetBird, Headscale, ZeroTier, Twingate,
  Cloudflare Tunnel sorted by use case. Multi-branch SMB, fully-remote
  team, self-host, per-resource ZTNA, L2 emulation, public exposure.
- [Tailscale vs WireGuard](https://meshwg.com/compare/tailscale-vs-wireguard/):
  protocol vs product. Tailscale IS WireGuard at the data plane.
- [Tailscale vs NetBird](https://meshwg.com/compare/tailscale-vs-netbird/):
  hosted-first vs self-host-first WireGuard mesh.
- [Tailscale vs ZeroTier](https://meshwg.com/compare/tailscale-vs-zerotier/):
  L3 WireGuard vs L2 Ethernet emulation; different design philosophies.
- [Tailscale vs Twingate](https://meshwg.com/compare/tailscale-vs-twingate/):
  mesh-first vs gateway-based ZTNA.
- [Tailscale vs Cloudflare Tunnel](https://meshwg.com/compare/tailscale-vs-cloudflare-tunnel/):
  bidirectional mesh vs one-way exposure.
- [Tailscale vs Headscale](https://meshwg.com/compare/tailscale-vs-headscale/):
  hosted Tailscale vs open-source self-hosted coordination.

## ZTNA (Zero Trust Network Access) cluster

- [What is ZTNA?](https://meshwg.com/what-is-ztna/): plain-English
  explainer of Zero Trust Network Access — definition, the VPN problem
  it solves, how the connector/policy-engine/client model works, the
  NIST 800-207 framing, ZTNA vs VPN vs mesh VPN, and an honest
  "do you actually need ZTNA" decision section.
- [ZTNA for small business](https://meshwg.com/ztna-for-small-business/):
  honest guide arguing most small businesses need a managed mesh VPN,
  not full ZTNA. Cost comparison ($7-15/user/mo ZTNA vs per-router
  mesh VPN), SMB-friendly options, decision framework by company size,
  and the three triggers that justify upgrading to pure ZTNA.
- [ZTNA vs VPN](https://meshwg.com/ztna-vs-vpn/): the implicit-vs-
  explicit-trust core difference, side-by-side comparison, the
  site-to-site job ZTNA structurally cannot do, and the mesh-VPN
  middle ground that has absorbed most of ZTNA's security benefits.

## WireGuard fundamentals + troubleshooting

- [What is WireGuard?](https://meshwg.com/what-is-wireguard/):
  plain-English explainer of the protocol; history; how it works;
  cryptographic choices (ChaCha20-Poly1305, Curve25519, BLAKE2s);
  vs OpenVPN and IPsec; supported platforms.
- [Why does my VPN keep disconnecting?](https://meshwg.com/why-vpn-keeps-disconnecting/):
  seven most common causes (NAT timeout, MTU clipping, ISP throttle,
  WiFi roam, kernel bugs, DNS, overnight rotation) with exact fixes.

## Competitor-vs-competitor comparisons (the matrix)

- [NetBird vs Headscale](https://meshwg.com/compare/netbird-vs-headscale/):
  two self-host WireGuard mesh paths — NetBird (complete BSD-3 product,
  commercial backing) vs Headscale (Tailscale-coordination re-implementation).
- [ZeroTier vs WireGuard](https://meshwg.com/compare/zerotier-vs-wireguard/):
  L2 Ethernet emulation vs the modern L3 kernel protocol; the
  "do you need Layer 2" decision.
- [Twingate vs NetBird](https://meshwg.com/compare/twingate-vs-netbird/):
  gateway ZTNA vs WireGuard mesh; per-resource access vs private network.
- [Twingate vs Cloudflare](https://meshwg.com/compare/twingate-vs-cloudflare/):
  focused best-of-breed ZTNA vs the Cloudflare One bundle;
  Cloudflare's free-50-user tier reshapes the decision.
- [Cloudflare Tunnel vs ngrok](https://meshwg.com/compare/cloudflare-tunnel-vs-ngrok/):
  persistent service exposure vs instant dev tunnels; and when neither
  fits because internal systems need a private network, not public exposure.

## Side-by-side comparisons

- [OPNsense vs pfSense WireGuard](https://meshwg.com/compare/opnsense-vs-pfsense-wireguard/):
  honest comparison covering kernel module vs userspace package
  on pfSense CE, throughput on identical hardware, licensing
  decision tree, and migration considerations between the two.
- [OpenWrt vs MikroTik WireGuard](https://meshwg.com/compare/openwrt-vs-mikrotik-wireguard/):
  free firmware on existing hardware vs purpose-built network
  hardware. Throughput by chipset class, configuration syntax
  comparison, mass-deployment scriptability.
- [WireGuard vs OpenVPN](https://meshwg.com/compare/wireguard-vs-openvpn/):
  speed (3-5× WireGuard win on identical hardware), security
  (attack surface, cryptographic primitives), configuration
  complexity, and three specific cases where OpenVPN still wins
  (TCP fallback, per-user auth, legacy integration).

    operational rollout playbook for SMBs deploying mesh VPN across
    5 to 50 branches. Covers a five-phase rollout (audit existing

    considerations, and real numbers from retail, clinic, and

  - [SD-WAN alternatives in 2026: seven modern options](https://meshwg.com/blog/sd-wan-alternatives-2026/):
    buyer's-guide listicle of seven modern alternatives to box-based

    protocol-level deep-dive into WireGuard site-to-site VPN. Covers the
    Noise_IK handshake, AllowedIPs / PersistentKeepalive semantics,
    multi-site (3+ peer) topologies including hub-and-spoke vs full mesh,

  - [TP-Link site-to-site VPN with WireGuard (2026)](https://meshwg.com/blog/tp-link-site-to-site-vpn-wireguard-2026/):
    vendor-specific tactical guide for connecting two, three, or thirty
    TP-Link branches over WireGuard. Covers Archer/Deco/ER/Omada paths,
    no-static-IP scenarios, multi-site mesh, WireGuard vs IPsec on TP-Link
    gear, and 20-branch cost economics. ~4,150 words, ~16 minute read.

## How signup works

- "Sign up free" buttons on meshwg.com route to https://vpn.meshwg.com/signup;
  "Sign in" routes to https://vpn.meshwg.com/login. Signup is self-serve
  and open to anyone.
- Two paths: email + password (with a 6-digit OTP email-verification step
  before first login), or "Continue with Google" for a one-click flow.
- Free tier: 2 machines per organisation, forever, no card required.
  Adding a 3rd machine prompts for a paid subscription via Razorpay
  (₹349/machine/month annual or ₹499/machine/month monthly, billed in INR).
- Corporate-domain routing: a signup from a domain another organisation
  has claimed (i.e. the founder of that org signed up first with the same
  domain) lands in that org's pending-approval queue rather than creating
  a duplicate. Freemail domains (gmail, yahoo, outlook, …) are always
  isolated — two strangers from gmail.com are never grouped.

## Key facts (for AI summarization)

- Product name: MeshWG
- Category: Hosted mesh VPN + zero-trust network access (ZTNA) for SMB and
  prosumer networks
- Underlying protocol: WireGuard (standard, RFC-style — no custom tunnel)
- Hardware requirement: None new. Works with routers from TP-Link,
  MikroTik, OpenWrt, Ubiquiti, OPNsense/pfSense, plus the official
  WireGuard apps on laptops/phones/servers.
- Isolation model: Each customer organisation is strictly isolated from
  every other organisation on the service. Other organisations cannot
  see or reach your machines, even if they happen to use overlapping
  private IP ranges.
- Policy model: Default-permit. Operators add explicit allow/deny rules
  scoped to source/destination machine, type (site/user), protocol, and
  port. When a policy denies traffic, packets are dropped before they
  reach the destination — there is no agent on the device to bypass.
- Pricing: 2 machines free forever. ₹349/machine/month annual or
  ₹499/machine/month monthly (INR, via Razorpay). Pro tier ("Talk to us")
  for dedicated infrastructure, custom domains, and SLA.
- Failure mode: WireGuard runs on the user's devices. If MeshWG is
  temporarily unreachable, existing tunnels keep working.
- Trademarks: WireGuard is a registered trademark of Jason A. Donenfeld.
